title: GLP-1 and Body-Weight Golden Evidence Map
research_question: Do GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce body weight in adults with overweight or obesity?

scope.population: Adults with overweight or obesity, with population extensions explicitly separated when diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, PMOS, or prior metabolic surgery changes applicability.
scope.intervention: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment, centered on semaglutide; liraglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide appear only as explicit endpoint, agent/population, or active-comparator context.
scope.outcome: Body-weight or anthropometric change during continued treatment and after documented treatment withdrawal; safety and non-weight outcomes appear only when they qualify what weight-loss efficacy does not establish.
scope.exclusions: No pediatric, pregnancy, cost-effectiveness, or class-wide safety conclusion is represented by this bounded map. Post-withdrawal durability is limited to one exploratory STEP 1 extension, and different primary outcomes are not treated as direct support or contradiction.

evidence_nodes.inclusion_rationale: Placebo-controlled STEP 5 evidence for semaglutide 2.4 mg at 104 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes.
Exploratory STEP 1 extension directly observing body-weight regain for 52 weeks after semaglutide and lifestyle-intervention withdrawal.
Large placebo-controlled SELECT analysis extending semaglutide weight and anthropometric outcomes to 208 weeks in adults with established cardiovascular disease without diabetes.
Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling randomized semaglutide trials while preserving dose, duration, and heterogeneity limitations.
Safety analysis from the same randomized-trial synthesis, preserving pooled adverse-event and discontinuation risks separately from body-weight efficacy.
Uncontrolled real-world semaglutide cohort extending observation to adults with obesity both with and without type 2 diabetes.
Propensity-matched oral-semaglutide cohort in adults with HFrEF, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, using no GLP-1 receptor agonist as comparator.
Short, uncontrolled PMOS cohort showing a distinct female reproductive population in which body weight is measured alongside ovulatory outcomes.

Large propensity-matched real-world comparison placing semaglutide weight-loss magnitude beside tirzepatide without reclassifying an active-comparator result as placebo-controlled support or contradiction.
Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing GLP-1RA-based and lifestyle intervention categories on waist circumference, an anthropometric outcome distinct from body weight.
Randomized secondary analysis showing that liraglutide's role in weight maintenance does not by itself establish improved physical fitness; exercise arms produced the fitness improvements.

Underpowered pilot RCT showing no additional six-month body-weight benefit from liraglutide 1.8 mg after gastric banding in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes; retained as an agent, population, dose, and surgical-context boundary rather than a same-PICO contradiction.

Single-arm, uncontrolled cohort of tirzepatide for recurrent weight gain after bariatric surgery or endoscopic bariatric therapy; extends agent and population coverage to a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist and a post-bariatric population without being directly comparable to STEP 5's randomized semaglutide result.

Large real-world retrospective cohort (n=69,049) finding that atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and digestive-system adverse events predict reduced first-year GLP-1 receptor agonist adherence; qualifies trial-based discontinuation findings with a drug-class-wide, real-world tolerability lens.

population_groups.label: Adults without diabetes in randomized semaglutide evidence
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: STEP 5 and Gao address general overweight or obesity eligibility; SELECT additionally requires established cardiovascular disease. These populations do not establish effects in adults with diabetes.

population_groups.label: Adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes or heart failure
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: These are observational extensions with different indications, formulations, and comparators; they do not erase the eligibility limits of the randomized semaglutide trials.

population_groups.label: Women with PMOS and elevated BMI
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: The PMOS cohort is uncontrolled and its distinguishing question concerns ovulatory function. Its body-weight finding is contextual, not evidence that STEP 5 or SELECT tested PMOS outcomes.

population_groups.label: Broader adult synthesis or post-diet weight-maintenance populations
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: The waist-circumference synthesis pools heterogeneous adult interventions, while the liraglutide analysis begins after diet-induced weight loss and evaluates fitness rather than primary weight reduction.

population_groups.label: Adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes after gastric banding
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: The small GLIDE pilot studied liraglutide 1.8 mg after laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding, with body weight as a secondary outcome. It cannot be substituted for semaglutide 2.4 mg evidence in non-surgical adults without diabetes.

population_groups.label: Adults with recurrent weight gain after bariatric surgery or endoscopic bariatric therapy
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: This cohort received tirzepatide, not semaglutide, after a prior bariatric procedure. It extends agent and population coverage but cannot be substituted for STEP 5's non-surgical, treatment-naive population.

population_groups.label: Broad real-world GLP-1 receptor agonist users across diabetes and obesity indications
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: This adherence cohort spans multiple GLP-1 receptor agonists and both diabetes and obesity indications rather than isolating semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity; its outcome is first-year adherence, not weight change.

comparator_groups.label: Placebo or randomized control
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The most direct comparative evidence, but behavioral co-intervention, trial eligibility, dose, duration, and pooled heterogeneity remain material.

comparator_groups.label: Withdrawal after randomized treatment
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The extension compares trajectories after both randomized study treatment and structured lifestyle intervention ended; it does not isolate medication withdrawal alone or establish every individual's course.

comparator_groups.label: Within-subject baseline without a concurrent control
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Observed change cannot isolate treatment effects from concurrent care, selection, regression to the mean, or other time-varying factors.

comparator_groups.label: No GLP-1 receptor agonist active-care comparator
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Propensity matching improves comparability but does not remove residual confounding or turn the cohort into a randomized placebo-controlled trial.

comparator_groups.label: Tirzepatide active comparator
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: A relative-effect comparison between two active therapies contextualizes magnitude; it does not refute semaglutide-versus-placebo evidence.

comparator_groups.label: Heterogeneous intervention categories
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Subgroup categories do not provide one uniform drug-versus-placebo estimate, and between-category differences were not statistically significant.

comparator_groups.label: Exercise and placebo factorial arms
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The finding qualifies fitness expectations during weight maintenance and must not be read as a null body-weight result.

comparator_groups.label: Post-gastric-banding placebo
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: GLIDE's placebo comparison occurs after laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding and against liraglutide 1.8 mg, not semaglutide 2.4 mg. Its underpowered null six-month body-weight result is an agent and population qualifier.

comparator_groups.label: Comorbidity subgroup comparison within one treated cohort
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The comparator is presence versus absence of a comorbidity (cardiovascular or digestive) within one real-world treated cohort, not a placebo or active-drug arm. It qualifies real-world tolerability, not efficacy or discontinuation rate.

contradiction_assessment.statement: A reproducible search completed on 2026-08-04 found no reviewed result that directly contradicts the semaglutide-versus-placebo body-weight direction under a sufficiently aligned population, intervention, comparator, outcome, and treatment window. GLIDE's underpowered null six-month result used liraglutide 1.8 mg after gastric banding in adults with type 2 diabetes and is an agent/population qualifier, not a same-PICO contradiction. Absence of an identified contradiction in this bounded search is not evidence that contradictory literature does not exist.

limitations: Secondary review verified record-to-source fidelity but did not independently reanalyze study data, perform a full risk-of-bias assessment, or establish source truth.

The direct randomized evidence is centered on semaglutide and adults without diabetes; one small liraglutide trial after gastric banding supplies a boundary but cannot support an undifferentiated class-wide conclusion for every GLP-1 receptor agonist or population.

Three population extensions, the active-comparator record, the post-bariatric tirzepatide qualifier, and the real-world adherence synthesis are observational and remain vulnerable to residual confounding.
Post-withdrawal durability is represented by one exploratory extension of selected STEP 1 completers and requires replication across agents, treatment durations, and longer follow-up.
The safety qualifier comes from one 2022 semaglutide review with varied doses and durations; it is not a current class-wide safety assessment or a benefit-harm conclusion.
Access, cost, patient preference, event severity, and individual benefit-harm tradeoffs are not represented.
The graph contains reviewed support and context links, but those links do not compute consensus or truth.
known_gaps: Human domain-expert adjudication remains available for disputed records or substantive future changes; this completed secondary audit was AI-assisted and is not human review.

Longer and independently replicated post-discontinuation trajectories across semaglutide and other agents remain open; the 2026-08-08 addition extended agent/population coverage (tirzepatide, post-bariatric) but did not add a second withdrawal-trajectory observation.

Broader agent-level coverage beyond semaglutide, with drug, dose, formulation, and duration kept separate; partially extended on 2026-08-08 by one tirzepatide post-bariatric cohort, still bounded to a single uncontrolled study.

Newer agent-specific and class-wide safety syntheses that preserve event severity, dose, duration, and population differences; partially extended on 2026-08-08 by one real-world adherence cohort, which measures adherence as a tolerability proxy rather than adjudicated adverse-event rates.
Pediatric, pregnancy, frailty, and geographically diverse population coverage where scientifically and ethically appropriate.

Periodic reruns of the same-PICO contradiction search as new trials mature or the direct map PICO changes; the 2026-08-04 bounded search identified none, and the 2026-08-08 addition of two agent/population and safety qualifiers did not surface a same-PICO contradiction either.

review.method: Independent source audit of every selected Evidence Record and Relationship Record against legally usable local PDFs, including durability, safety, and agent/population qualifiers, with explicit PICO, comparator, time-window, endpoint, numerical result, limitation, relationship-rationale, and contradiction-boundary checks.
review.notes: The initial audit corrected two Evidence Records and two relationship rationales; the durability/safety follow-up added two source-audited Evidence Records and three reviewed qualifier relationships; the same-PICO contradiction audit added one source-audited agent/population qualifier and one reviewed relationship while preserving an honest negative search result. The 2026-08-08 gap-closure round added two further source-audited Evidence Records already at manual_human_review extraction tier (a post-bariatric tirzepatide cohort and a real-world GLP-1RA adherence/comorbidity cohort) and two reviewed relationships (contextualizes, qualifies), each independently re-verified against its source PDF this round; it is a bounded partial closure of the durability/agent-coverage/safety-synthesis gaps, not a full resolution of any of them. Reviewed means accepted for record-to-source fidelity under the map contract. It does not mean human domain-expert approval, independent statistical reanalysis, scientific synthesis, benefit-harm assessment, consensus, confidence, or truth determination.
